callouts.text: 1 · Click "pose: Pose" to expand it in place. Click the nested "x: Pose" again to go deeper — Pose is self-referential, so there is no depth limit.
2 · Double-click the "quality: float" row (or any row) to drop straight into Source mode with your cursor placed exactly where you clicked.
3 · Same engine as V1 — leading chevron (before the name) and a solid guide rail down the nested column.
4 · Same engine again — trailing chevron (like V1) with a dotted guide instead of a solid rail.

Note · In Source mode on any of these (or the Mapping below), start a new line or edit a type and type a partial name. A dropdown anchored under your cursor suggests board types (purple pill), Type Mappings (orange pill) and Python primitives (grey pill), ranked by relevance — with a "show every type" link to browse the whole board.
5 · Click the blue "Pose" token inside the expression — it jumps the camera to the real Pose block above, confirming a Mapping resolves against live board Types.

6 · Click Source, then position your cursor inside "Callable[[Frame, float], Po|" and keep typing — the same autocomplete matches an identifier anywhere inside a nested expression, not just right after a colon.

PASS WHEN · Expanding stays instant at any depth (no reselecting needed to see a fresh default value), double-click lands the cursor where you clicked, the Mapping token jump selects the real Pose block, and typing a partial name in either editor's Source mode opens a colored-pill autocomplete dropdown.
